name: wrcoef
expr: a3 = wrcoef('a', c, l, 'haar', 3); a2 = wrcoef('a', c, l, 'haar', 2); a1 = wrcoef('a', c, l, 'haar', 1); a0 = wrcoef('a', c, l, 'haar', 0); d3 = wrcoef('d', c, l, 'haar', 3); d2 = wrcoef('d', c, l, 'haar', 2); d1 = wrcoef('d', c, l, 'haar', 1); a_def = wrcoef('a', c, l, 'haar'); d_def = wrcoef('d', c, l, 'haar'); recon = a3 + d1 + d2 + d3; ident_max = max(abs(recon - a0));
comment: Sig: y = wrcoef(type, c, l, wname[, n]). Single-band reconstruction. type ∈ {'a','d'}; n is the level kept ('a' allows n=0 = full reconstruction; 'd' requires n in [1, max]). Default n = length(l)-2 for both types. Algorithm: build modified c with off-band coefficients zeroed, run waverec. Verified parity with MATLAB R2025b on HAAR wavelet (where numkit's wavedec matches MATLAB exactly). For db/sym/coif numkit's wavedec uses a slightly different boundary convention (BUGS.md #37) — wrcoef there produces values consistent with numkit's own wavedec/waverec round-trip but does NOT match MATLAB coefficient-for-coefficient. (Lo_R, Hi_R) two-filter form not implemented in this release.
